newsitem.title: USA: Baby's family to have say in British nanny's case.
newsitem.headline: Baby's family to have say in British nanny's case.

text.p: The family of a 9-month-old boy who died after allegedly being shaken by his British nanny will help determine what additional charges she faces, including murder or manslaughter, prosecutors said on Monday.

Louise Woodward, 18, who came to the United States in June from her home in Chester, England, is already being held on $100,000 cash bail on a charge of assault and battery. She was arrested one day after the infant, Matthew Eappen, was taken to Children's Hospital in Boston suffering from head injuries.
The boy, who had been on life support, died on Sunday night of an intracranial haemorrhage. Prosecutors told reporters last week they would seek murder charges against Woodward if the baby died.

But on Monday, Middlesex District Attorney Thomas Reilly declined to discuss what further charges would be brought against Woodward, saying: "We have made no decision yet. Yes, there is the probability there will be additional charges."
He said great weight was given to the wishes of the victim's family in his county. "They have input into what we do. At this point, I see no reason to rush into this."
Reilly said his office would "be speaking to doctors and review the case and make a decision at a later time. Right now, this is a time of mourning for the family. Tremendous loss for that family."

Eappen's parents, Drs. Sunil and Deborah Eappen, said in a statement released through Children's Hospital: "We would like to thank our families and many friends for their overwhelming support and prayers. Matthew was a tremendous gift and joy to us, and he will forever be a part of our lives."
The blinds were drawn on their white Cape Cod-style home with toys and a baby carriage (pram) on the porch, in the upscale town of Newton, about a 15-minute drive from Boston.
"I feel I've already lost my daughter and I've at least got the hope of getting her back. I can't imagine how they would feel," Woodward's mother told reporters in England.
The Eappens were the second Massachusetts family to employ Woodward. She previously worked for Harris and Lauren Komishane in Manchester-by-the-Sea, about an hour's drive northeast of Boston.

"It's just unbelievable," Harris Komishane told reporters, explaining that a disagreement over curfews led to Woodward's departure from his employ. He said there were "absolutely no problems" with Woodward's work.
